sentences.text:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice Sindhu Sharma, Judge
 Order

This Court, vide order dated 23.02.2024, was of the view that compensation payable to the petitioners could be settled by negotiations and mutual consent and further held that since the amount of Rs.25.645 lacs had already been assessed as compensation payable to the petitioners by the Executive Engineer and the same was acceptable to the petitioners as well, it would be in the fitness of the things, if the matter is settled at the said amount and the title of subject property was transferred by the petitioners to the Public Works Department by executing a deed of conveyance.
The Court further directed the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Mahore, and Executive Engineer, PWD (R&B) Special Sub-Division, Mahore, and also the petitioners to remain present before this Court today.

02. The petitioners are present in person and also Sh. Mazahir Hussain Shah, Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Mahore, and Sh. Rajesh Kumar, Executive Engineer, PWD (R&B) Special Sub-Division,
Mahore, are present in person.
03. The Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Mahore, submits that only 5 Kanal and 13 Marlas of land belonging to the petitioners was utilized by the respondents for the construction of a road.
Out of this, 1 Kanal and 2  Marlas belong to petitioner No. 1, and 1 Kanal and 17 Marlas belong to petitioner No. 2
and submits that there are other co-sharers also in the said land.

He further submits Ashoo Begum And Another vs State Of J&K And Others on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86674504/
1 that he has received the indent for acquisition of land under the Fair Compensation Act.

sentences.text: 04. It would be appropriate for the parties to negotiate and settle the dispute regarding the compensation due and payable to them in terms of order dated 23.02.2024.

The Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Mahore, may convene a meeting in presence of the representatives of the petitioner and also the Executive Engineer concerned, for discussing/settling the matter and provide instructions about the same on the next date of hearing.

05. Keeping in view the fact that petitioner No. 1 is ninety-five years old and petitioner No. 2 is seventy years old, the respondents are directed to release the compensation due to them for their shares of land before the Registry by the next date of hearing.

(Sindhu Sharma) Judge Jammu:
